questions.q: What IS this feature in one sentence?
questions.a: Controls how PCG volumes spawn biome-specific resource pickup actors across the level surface based on biome type and density.

questions.q: What wider system does it belong to?
questions.a: The biome_resources rung, which governs what resources exist and where in each biome zone.

questions.q: What would break if this feature didn't exist?
questions.a: Resources would need to be hand-placed by a human level designer — no procedural spawn, no dynamic replenishment.

questions.q: What existing feature does this most resemble?
questions.a: ground_terrain (both use PCG volumes for procedural placement of world elements).

questions.q: Is this a rung, a sub-rung, or a parameter?
questions.a: Sub-rung auto-decomposed from biome_resources.

questions.q: What physical constraint does it encode?
questions.a: Resource density per biome type: desert has 0.3 sand rocks per m^2, arctic has 0.1 ice crystals per m^2, etc.

questions.q: What is the ONE measurement that proves it works?
questions.a: When a PCG volume generates for a biome, the resource actor count per 100m^2 matches the biome's density profile within ±5% across 5+ generations.

questions.q: What wall must it never violate?
questions.a: Must never spawn a resource inside a shelter volume or within 2m of a non-PCG-placed actor (player-start, beacon, NPC spawn).

questions.q: What would a degenerate winner look like?
questions.a: A PCG volume that spawns 1000 resources in a 10m^2 pile, or one that spawns zero resources because the density fell below the spawn threshold.

questions.q: How would we know if the constraint is too loose?
questions.a: If all biomes spawn the same resource density (no differentiation), the PCG density constraint is too loose.

questions.q: At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Per-PCG-volume, evaluated once during level generation (each biome region gets one volume pass).

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
questions.a: Parameter-level: 5 variables (density_per_biome_map, spawn_min_dist, overlap_cull_radius, replenish_interval_sec, max_spawns_per_volume).

questions.q: Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Could split density_per_biome_map into 8 separate per-biome density parameters, but a single mapping parameter is more portable.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: Pattern emerges after 3 PCG volume generations when each biome zone shows visibly different resource density.

questions.q: What would 'deep enough' look like for this feature?
questions.a: When biome resource density clusters match player expectation: desert feels sparse (few scattered rocks), forest feels dense (clusters of branches).

questions.q: What element catalog variables does this train?
questions.a: pcg_density_mult, spawn_exclusion_radius, resource_actor_type_map, replenish_timer_sec.

questions.q: How many relevant elements exist in the catalog?
questions.a: 53 catalog entries tagged 'pcg' and 'resource_spawner' in the 69,749-element catalog.

questions.q: Are there enough variables to train meaningfully?
questions.a: Yes — 5 parameters with 53 catalog elements provide rich constraint space.

questions.q: What variables are MISSING from the catalog?
questions.a: Per-resource-type exclusion rules (e.g., avoid water surfaces) — currently using a global exclusion radius.

questions.q: Would training this require GPU acceleration?
questions.a: No — 5 variables is far below the 1000-variable GPU threshold.

questions.q: Does this feature connect to the Mirror of Erised?
questions.a: Enabling — PCG resource spawning creates the material conditions for giving. No spawned resources = nothing to give.

questions.q: How directly does it serve the Mirror? (direct/enabling/orthogonal)
questions.a: Enabling — without spawned resources the give/receive loop has nothing to transact.

questions.q: Would a costless life still be meaningful without this feature?
questions.a: No — if resources must be hand-placed the world feels authored, not emergent. The Mirror needs the world to feel alive.

questions.q: Could this feature be gamed to fake a generous life?
questions.a: No — resource spawn density is indifferent to player behavior. The player cannot force more spawns.

questions.q: What would this feature look like if it perfectly served the Mirror?
questions.a: Every biome has enough resources for its NPC needs. The player can always find something to give, but never so much that giving costs nothing.

questions.q: What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: biome_resources (parent), ground_terrain (PCG surface overlap), resource_pickup (actor type to spawn).

questions.q: What could break at the seam between this and its neighbors?
questions.a: PCG spawns a resource inside a terrain height cliff face because the exclusion check doesn't account for vertical surfaces.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step to place in the level?
questions.a: No — PCG volumes run at editor time and auto-place resources. The decoder needs to ensure the PCG volume exists with the right biome assignment.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
questions.a: ground_terrain PCG and biome_resources PCG both claim the same space — resources float in the air because terrain was sculpted after spawn.

questions.q: Does this feature need a human judgment or can the system verify it?
questions.a: System verifies density and exclusion. Human judges whether the resource distribution looks natural (not in grid patterns, not clumped in UI-obscuring piles).

questions.q: How many generations to converge?
questions.a: ~60 generations at pop=64 for 5-parameter PCG density constraint.

questions.q: What population size is appropriate?
questions.a: 64 — PCG distribution benefits from larger population to explore spatial patterns.

questions.q: What's the risk of overfitting?
questions.a: Medium — a winner could memorize specific spawn coordinates for one terrain seed and fail on a different seed.

questions.q: What's the risk of underfitting?
questions.a: Medium — if density parameters are too coarse, all biomes get the same resource pattern.

questions.q: Does the existing trainer support this domain type?
questions.a: Yes — core.trainer handles spatial density constraints with Python simulation (CPU).

questions.q: Have we gone deep enough on this feature?
questions.a: Yes — 5 parameters with exclusion walls cover the PCG resource distribution space adequately.

questions.q: What would the NEXT level of decomposition look like?
questions.a: Per-biome PCG subgraph generation: one dedicated PCG graph for each of the 8 biome types with unique noise patterns.

questions.q: If we stopped here, would the game feel complete?
questions.a: Partially — resources would be procedurally placed but might look same-y across biomes.

questions.q: What is the human's expected emotional response to this feature?
questions.a: Exploratory curiosity — 'every biome has different stuff on the ground. What does THIS place offer?'

questions.q: Does this feature exist because the Mirror demands it, or because it's technically interesting?
questions.a: Both — PCG resource placement is technically elegant and it's the substrate for the entire give/receive economy.
